 Petrol price slashed by Rs5.45, diesel rate reduced by Rs3.68 per litre
 Petrol will now cost Rs369.06 per litre, while high-speed diesel will be sold at Rs391.52
 Business 
 By   Saif Ur Rehman 
 November 03, 2026 
 A worker holds a fuel nozzle to fill fuel in a car at a petrol station in Karachi, on September 16, 2023. — Reuters The federal government on Tuesday announced a cut of Rs5.45 per litre in petrol prices and Rs3.68 per litre in high-speed diesel (HSD) rates.
 Following the reduction, petrol will be sold at Rs369.06 per litre, while the price of high-speed diesel has been decreased to Rs391.52 per litre.
 According to a notification issued by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA), the revised rates will remain effective until November 4.
 Ogra has also begun publishing daily petroleum prices on its website to improve transparency and allow changes in international oil prices to be passed on to consumers more quickly.
 Here are fuel rates: 
 Effective date Products Old rates New rates Change in prices 
 Nov 4 Petrol 374.51 369.06 -5.45 
 Nov 4 High-speed diesel 395.20 391.52 -3.68 
 Amid heightened volatility in global oil markets following renewed hostilities in the Middle East, the government decided to adopt a daily fuel price review mechanism.
 The weekly review system had been introduced after the outbreak of the Israel-Iran conflict in February, which was further intensified by US involvement and disruptions to energy shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil supplies.
 Prior to the weekly mechanism, petroleum prices were revised on a fortnightly basis.
 How revised petrol pricing works 
 The federal cabinet approved changes to the petrol pricing mechanism on October 30 amid volatility caused by the US-Iran war.
 Under the revised formula, the import price of petrol is determined on the basis of the actual import cost of the relevant PSO cargo. If that cost is unavailable for daily pricing, the premium, incidentals and customs duty of the last available cargo are used instead.
 For local refineries, the government has temporarily fixed the premium, incidentals and customs duty used in calculating the ex-refinery petrol price at their March 7, 2026 — pre-war — levels for 30 days.
 The difference between the import price and the resulting ex-refinery price is to be surrendered by refineries under the petroleum levy account, with the resulting benefit passed on through a corresponding reduction in the petrol price.
 The government has also introduced a short-term adjustment to smooth petrol price movements, incorporating the benefit arising from a premium differential into petrol prices at a rate of $2.950 per barrel per day.
